summary: The note recounts Karachi's response to a severe rainstorm and flood on September 5, 2023, highlighting individual, NGO, business and international efforts in rescue and recovery. It also covers plans to strengthen infrastructure and build a flood-resilient city by 2025, framing the disaster as an opportunity for growth.
one_line: After the September 5, 2023 Karachi flood, residents, NGOs, businesses and foreign experts rallied to rescue, rebuild and plan a flood-resilient city.
key_facts: On September 5, 2023, an intense rainstorm hit Karachi, with an unprecedented 300 millimeters of rainfall in just 24 hours.
Karachi is described as Pakistan's economic hub and has long suffered flooding from heavy monsoon rains.
Asim Hussain, a 40-year-old street vendor, used a makeshift raft originally used to transport merchandise to carry food and water to people trapped by flooding, despite losing his stall.
Fatima Khalid, a 25-year-old teacher whose school was ruined, turned her small apartment into a classroom for the community's children.
The NGO "One Hand", led by social worker Raza Ahmed, used social media to coordinate rescues, map worst-hit areas and distribute aid, with precision that government agencies struggled to match.
Samina Ali of a prominent textile firm redirected resources to produce blankets and clothing for those left without aid, as part of a wider corporate movement.
Public and private sectors joined a resilient urban framework project led by city planner Hasan Iqbal, focused on drainage systems, solid waste management and sustainable urban landscaping.
Hasan Iqbal said "Karachi must not only recover, but become an example in urban resilience" and presented a plan for a flood-resilient Karachi by 2025.
Experts from the Netherlands, known for water management, collaborated with local authorities and provided expertise for rebuilding.
Dr. Sameera Javed led medical professionals in setting up mobile clinics to help prevent waterborne disease outbreaks.
"Green Karachi" is a youth initiative led by university students to increase urban green spaces and foster environmental awareness.
The note says the 2023 monsoon season highlighted an urgent need to fix infrastructural deficiencies.
